evidence.title: Dokos Early Helladic Shipwreck (Hydra Strait, Greece)
evidence.dateBasis: Relative pottery typology (Early Helladic II sauceboats and askoi) recovered from 18–32 m depth off Dokos Island.
evidence.summary: Oldest excavated cargo wreck in the eastern Mediterranean (~500 ceramic vessels, stone anchors, and millstones carried by an Aegean coastal trader; wooden hull perished on rocky seabed).
evidence.limits: Timber hull structure did not survive; date relies on ceramic typology rather than timber radiocarbon.

evidence.title: Kumluca & Kekova Bronze Age Ingot Shipwrecks (Antalya, Turkey)
evidence.dateBasis: Morphology of 30+ copper pillow/oxhide ingots and associated Middle–Late Bronze transition ceramics along the Lycian coast.
evidence.summary: Early and Middle-to-Late Bronze Age wrecks off Kumluca and Kekova preserving Cyprus/Anatolian copper ingots predating Uluburun, demonstrating early bulk metal transport along southern Anatolia.
evidence.limits: Dating of Kumluca (16th c. BCE) and nearby Early Bronze Kekova finds remains ongoing as underwater excavations progress.

evidence.title: Cape Gelidonya Bronze Age Tinkering & Copper Wreck (Lycia, Turkey)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon on dunnage brushwood and Mycenaean IIIB/Syro-Palestinian pottery typology.
evidence.summary: Late Bronze Age Syrian-Cypriot merchantman carrying ~1 ton of oxhide/bun copper ingots, tin ingots, scrap bronze for shipboard recycling, cylinder seals, and pan-balance weights.
evidence.limits: Only small brushwood dunnage and hull planking traces survived on rocky bottom.

evidence.title: Point Iria Cypriot-Mycenaean Cargo Wreck (Argolid Gulf, Greece)
evidence.dateBasis: Comparative LH IIIB2 / Cypriot LC IIC pithoi and stirrup-jar typology.
evidence.summary: Three-origin ceramic assemblage linking Cyprus, Crete, and the Mycenaean Argolid around the Late Bronze Age palace collapse, demonstrating resilient maritime networks after ~1200 BCE.
evidence.limits: Hull timbers lost; vessel size and ethnic identity of crew remain inferred from cargo provenance.

evidence.title: Mazarrón 1 & 2 Phoenician Merchantmen (Murcia, Spain)
evidence.dateBasis: Phoenician R-1 amphorae, wood AMS radiocarbon, and stratigraphic burial in Playa de la Isla sands.
evidence.summary: Rare intact Archaic Phoenician coasters (~8.15 m long) preserving sewn-and-mortised Aleppo pine planking waterproofed with resin and carrying litharge (silver-refining lead) ingots in Iberia.
evidence.limits: Represent small coastal cabotage craft rather than long-haul Trans-Mediterranean ocean freighters.

evidence.title: Bajo de la Campana Phoenician Ivory & Tin Wreck (Murcia, Spain)
evidence.dateBasis: Carthage/Western Phoenician amphora typology and raw elephant tusks inscribed in Phoenician script.
evidence.summary: Deep-water cargo wreck carrying ~50 inscribed African elephant tusks, pine cones, galena ore, tin, copper ingots, and ornate Phoenician bronze furniture elements toward Atlantic/SE Iberia.
evidence.limits: Vessel hull fragmented on shallow reef shoal; attribution relies on cargo signatures.

evidence.title: Giglio Campese Archaic Etruscan-Greek Wreck (Tuscany, Italy)
evidence.dateBasis: Corinthian helmets, Laconian craters, Etruscan bucchero & Samian amphorae, plus mortise-and-laced keel timbers.
evidence.summary: Archaic Tyrrhenian merchantman carrying composite elite gifts and commodities (tar pitch bins, olive jars, iron bars, copper ingots, Corinthian armor, and flute tubes) in a mixed laced-and-mortised hull.
evidence.limits: Steep rocky slope dispersal mixed some shallower intrusive sherds with the main cargo.

evidence.title: Jules-Verne 7 & 9 Sewn-Plank Massaliote Boats (Marseille, France)
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology and harbor silt stratigraphy in Place Jules-Verne (ancient Massalia).
evidence.summary: Abandoned port vessels recording the pivotal Mediterranean shipwright transition: Jules-Verne 9 uses traditional Archaic vegetable-fiber lacing, whereas Jules-Verne 7 introduces pinned mortise-and-tenon joinery.
evidence.limits: Scuttled/discarded port boats rather than deep-water open-sea cargo wrecks.

evidence.title: Ma'agan Mikhael Late Classical Merchantman (Carmel Coast, Israel)
evidence.dateBasis: East Aegean/Cypriot basket-handle amphorae, Attic black-glaze pottery, and radiocarbon of shipwright basketry & rope.
evidence.summary: Extraordinarily preserved 13.8 m pine merchantman with shipwright woodworking toolkit, ~13 tonnes of Euboean gabbro ballast, a rare one-armed wooden anchor with lead stock, and Cyprus-type wine jars.
evidence.limits: Cargo was modest near-empty voyage stores rather than full commercial consignment.

evidence.title: Black Sea MAP Anoxic Classical Greek Merchantman (off Burgas, Bulgaria)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dating by Black Sea Maritime Archaeology Project (at >2,000 m depth).
evidence.summary: Intact 23 m Classical Greek trading vessel resting upright on the hydrogen-sulfide anoxic Black Sea floor with mast, rudders, rowing benches, and rigging rope still attached.
evidence.limits: Deep-water ROV study without full hull raising leaves hold interior cargo largely unexcavated.

evidence.title: Kyrenia Hellenistic Almond & Amphora Freighter (Northern Cyprus)
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology (~389 BCE felling), Rhodes amphora stamps, Demetrius Poliorcetes bronze coins, and cargo radiocarbon.
evidence.summary: Iconic 14 m Aleppo pine merchantman sheathed in protective lead sheets, carrying ~400 Rhodian wine amphorae, ~10,000 preserved almonds, Nisyros grain millstones, and crew tableware.
evidence.limits: Timber was already ~80–90 years old at sinking due to long working vessel life and repairs.

evidence.title: Egadi Islands First Punic War Rams & Marsala Punic Warships (Sicily)
evidence.dateBasis: Latin quaestor inscriptions on 25+ bronze naval rams from the 10 March 241 BCE Battle of the Egadi Islands + Punic alphabetical hullwright marks on Marsala wreck.
evidence.summary: First archaeological battle-fleet horizon in antiquity: over two dozen cast bronze naval rams, Montefortino helmets, and nearby Carthaginian Marsala light oared warship timbers.
evidence.limits: Bronze rams and helmets preserve combat loss lines while hull timbers survived only in protected Lilybaeum lagoon sediments.

evidence.title: Mahdia Late Hellenistic Sunken Sculpture Cargo (Tunisia)
evidence.dateBasis: Attic bronze inscriptions, Neo-Attic marble crater styling, and Athens Piraeus coin issues (~86–70 BCE).
evidence.summary: Deep-water (~40 m) freighter storm-blown off course between Attica and Italy carrying ~70 unfinished Pentelic marble columns (~200 tons), bronze Agon and Herm statues by Boethos, and ornate bronze klinai couches.
evidence.limits: Early 1907–1913 sponge-diver salvage predated stratified stratigraphic recording standards.

evidence.title: Madrague de Giens Roman Double-Planked Wine Freighter (Var, France)
evidence.dateBasis: Terracina Caecuban & Falernian Dressel 1B amphorae stamps (Publius Veveius Papus) and Campanian black-gloss wares.
evidence.summary: Monumental 40 m, ~400-ton double-planked shell-first Roman merchantman carrying ~6,000–7,000 Italian wine amphorae (~400 tons) plus deck crates of Arretine/Campanian ceramics toward Gaul.
evidence.limits: Heavy salvage attempts occurred in antiquity shortly after sinking.

evidence.title: Antikythera Wreck & Astronomical Geared Mechanism (Greece)
evidence.dateBasis: Pergamene & Ephesian silver cistophori coins (~86–67 BCE), Lagynos ware, and internal gearing/Saros eclipse calendar dates.
evidence.summary: Luxurious eastern Mediterranean merchantman bearing ~36 marble statues, bronze Philosopher & Youth sculptures, blown mosaic glass bowls, and the 30+ bronze geared astronomical computer (Antikythera Mechanism).
evidence.limits: Steep 50 m sea-cliff shelf compressed stratigraphy; new geoarchaeological surveys continue clarifying hull extent.

evidence.title: Comacchio Roman Adriatic Lead-Ingot Merchantman (Ferrara, Italy)
evidence.dateBasis: Spanish Carthago Nova lead ingots stamped with Agrippa/Tiberian marks and Augustan terra sigillata.
evidence.summary: Nearly intact 21 m flat-bottomed Po-Adriatic coastal trader (sewn top-strakes over mortised hull) carrying 102 stamped Spanish lead ingots, boxwood temples, and shipboard Lararium shrine.
evidence.limits: Recovered from reclaimed Po Delta lagoon channel silts; transitional hybrid sewn/mortised hull construction.

evidence.title: Pisa–San Rossore Silted Harbor Fleet (Tuscany, Italy)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified flood-avulsion muds of ancient Auser/Arno branch yielding >30 complete and partial hulls from Republican to Late Antique dates.
evidence.summary: Pompeii of ancient shipbuilding: >30 river-and-sea vessels entombed rapidly by catastrophic floods—from Hellenistic cargo freighters (Nave B) and thirty-meter warships (Alkedo) to tiny river skiffs with preserved ropes and passenger baggage.
evidence.limits: Multi-century cumulative harbor disaster horizon rather than one simultaneous sinking.

evidence.title: Yassıada 4th- & 7th-Century Roman/Byzantine Wrecks (Bodrum, Turkey)
evidence.dateBasis: Coin issues of Heraclius (latest 625/626 CE) and Late Roman Amphora 1/2 cargo typologies.
evidence.summary: Landmark benchmark wrecks showing the crucial transition from Greco-Roman shell-first mortise-and-tenon hull construction to early medieval frame-first skeleton construction.
evidence.limits: Spans two distinct wrecks separated by ~250 years on the same treacherous Aegean reef.

evidence.title: Ma'agan Mikhael B Late Byzantine–Early Islamic Wreck (Israel)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon on walnuts/twigs, pottery LRA 4/5/7 & Umayyad glassware, and early frame-first walnut/fir construction.
evidence.summary: 20 m coastal merchantman trading along the early Islamic Levantine coast with LRA 5 bag amphorae, olives, walnuts, glass vessels, and iron tools built primarily frame-first.
evidence.limits: Overlies a wide 7th–8th century radiocarbon calibration window across Umayyad continuity.

evidence.title: Bozburun Middle Byzantine Wine Amphora Wreck (Caria, Turkey)
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology on Turkish oak hull timbers (felling ~874 CE) and Crimean/Black Sea-type Günsenin Class I amphorae.
evidence.summary: Middle Byzantine freighter (~15 m) carrying >1,200 wine amphorae stamped with ecclesiastical/estate monograms, built entirely frame-first with iron nails along Aegean–Black Sea routes.
evidence.limits: Upper port side eroded; internal oak framing preserved under amphora overburden.

evidence.title: Khufu Cedar Solar Barque (Giza, Egypt)
evidence.dateBasis: Old Kingdom Fourth Dynasty royal boat pit sealed by limestone blocks bearing cartouches of Djedefre.
evidence.summary: 43.4 m ceremonial/seagoing-type Lebanese cedar vessel disassembled into 1,224 lashed/mortised pieces beside the Great Pyramid—oldest intact planked ship architecture on Earth.
evidence.limits: Ritually buried in a desert stone pit rather than lost at sea.

evidence.title: Wadi al-Jarf & Mersa/Wadi Gawasis Red Sea Boat Galleries (Egypt)
evidence.dateBasis: Old Kingdom Khufu logbook papyri (Wadi al-Jarf) & Middle Kingdom 12th Dynasty harbor stelae/cedar planks (Wadi Gawasis).
evidence.summary: Pharaonic Red Sea rock-cut shipworm-scarred cedar hull caves & rigging coils disassembled after Punt & Sinai voyages, proving modular prefabricated ocean vessels hauled across the Eastern Desert.
evidence.limits: Reused timber caches and harbor galleries spans Old Kingdom copper voyages (29°N) and Middle Kingdom Punt fleets (26.5°N).

evidence.title: Thonis-Heracleion Ship 17 (Herodotus' Baris) & Harbor Fleet (Egypt)
evidence.dateBasis: Submerged Nile-mouth port stratigraphy and exact plank-joinery match to Herodotus Book 2.96.
evidence.summary: Excavation of 70+ sunken boats in Aboukir Bay, led by Ship 17—the first archaeological verification of the Egyptian Acacia nilotica 'baris' described by Herodotus with long internal tenons pinned through ribs.
evidence.limits: Submerged delta harbor deposits mix purposeful ritual boat scuttlings with working freighters.

evidence.title: Sea of Galilee Wooden Fishing Boat (Ginosar, Israel)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dating, Herod-period oil lamp & cooking pot inside lake mud, and Roman-era repair carpentry.
evidence.summary: 8.2 m cedar-and-oak freshwater rowing/sailing fishing skiff preserved in anoxic Kinneret lake clay with recycled timbers from older hulls and shell-first pegged mortises.
evidence.limits: Abandoned/stripped hulk sunk deliberately in shallow mud after service life ended.

evidence.title: Ferriby 1–3 Early Bronze Age Sewn-Plank Boats (Humber, England)
evidence.dateBasis: High-precision AMS radiocarbon on yew withy stitches and oak bottom cleats (2030–1680 cal BCE range).
evidence.summary: World's oldest known ocean-capable European sewn-plank boats (up to ~16 m oak hulls stitched with twisted yew withies and caulked with moss), demonstrating Bronze Age Channel & North Sea navigation.
evidence.limits: Tidal Humber foreshore preserves bottom and lower strakes; upper sides lost to erosion.

evidence.title: Dover Middle Bronze Age Cross-Channel Sewn Boat (Kent, England)
evidence.dateBasis: Wiggle-matched radiocarbon on yew stitches and oak planks (~1575–1520 cal BCE).
evidence.summary: Excavated in buried Dour estuary sediments: heavy carved oak bottom and cleat hull (>9.5 m recovered) stitched with yew twisted cords, Kimmeridge shale cargo associations, and experimental Channel seaworthiness.
evidence.limits: Stern/prow ends truncated by modern sewer works and ancient abandonment dismantling.

evidence.title: Hjortspring Pre-Roman Iron Age Sewn War Canoe (Als, Denmark)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon on limewood hull, pine-pitch caulking, and ~150 iron spearheads/mail coats deposited as war sacrifice.
evidence.summary: 19 m limewood double-prowed war vessel (crew ~22 paddlers) sewn exclusively with plant bast cordage (no iron fasteners in hull), containing captured shields, mail armor, and weapons—oldest Baltic plank boat.
evidence.limits: Ritual bog weapon-sacrifice deposition (~4th c. BCE) leaves provenance of defeated raiders debated.

evidence.title: Zwammerdam Roman Rhine Limes Fleet Barges (Netherlands)
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology on Roman oak barges and dugouts beside Nigrum Pullum fort along the Lower Germanic Limes.
evidence.summary: Six intact Roman river vessels (up to 34 m flat-bottomed 'praams') hauling stone, grain, and legionary supplies along the Rhine delta frontier.
evidence.limits: Fluvial river barges reflecting frontier military logistics rather than deep-sea voyages.

evidence.title: Blackfriars 1 Romano-Celtic Stone Freighter (London, England)
evidence.dateBasis: Worn Domitianic bronze coin (88/89 CE) intentionally placed under the mast-step plus Kentish Ragstone cargo for Londinium walls.
evidence.summary: 18.5 m sturdy flat-bottomed frame-built Celtic/Romano-British sailing freighter sunk in the Thames laden with ~26 tonnes of Kentish building stone and a millstone.
evidence.limits: Upper deck lost; illustrates indigenous Atlantic/Celtic non-Mediterranean framing beside Roman administration.

evidence.title: Nydam Oak Clinker Warship (Southern Jutland, Denmark)
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology (oak felled 310–320 CE) from Migration-Period bog sacrifice.
evidence.summary: 23 m clinker-built (overlapping iron-riveted oak planks) 30-oared warship—earliest intact ancestor of the Norse Viking longship, sacrificed alongside Roman-Germanic swords and runic fittings.
evidence.limits: Oar-propelled warship lacking a true stepped mast; sacrificed ~340–350 CE after Baltic warfare.

evidence.title: Oseberg & Gokstad Viking Clinker Ship Burials (Vestfold, Norway)
evidence.dateBasis: Exact tree-ring felling dates (Oseberg burial summer 834 CE; Gokstad burial ~901–905 CE).
evidence.summary: Opulently carved 21.5 m Oseberg ceremonial/coastal craft and ocean-going 23.8 m Gokstad warship buried under blue clay mounds—benchmarks of flexible clinker hydrodynamics and Viking Age elite navigation.
evidence.limits: Deliberate high-status royal mound burials on land rather than working shipwreck loss.

evidence.title: Skuldelev 1–6 Viking-Age Blockade Ships (Roskilde Fjord, Denmark)
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology identifying oak & pine origins in Dublin (Skuldelev 2, 1042 CE), Sognefjord (Skuldelev 1), and Denmark.
evidence.summary: Five specialized Late Viking vessels deliberately stone-sunk to block the Peberrenden channel (~1070 CE): a Dublin-built 30 m dragonship, North Atlantic knarr ocean freighter, Baltic merchant trader, and coastal fishing craft.
evidence.limits: Intentional harbor defense scuttling rather than accidental storm wrecking.

evidence.title: Bremen Hanseatic Oak Cog (Weser River, Germany)
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology confirming oak felled in autumn 1378 CE, swept away by river flood near completion ~1380.
evidence.summary: Nearly complete 24 m flat-bottomed Hanseatic bulk freighter with sternpost pintle rudder, high castled stern, and single square rig (~200-ton capacity) that anchored Baltic-North Sea grain, salt, and cloth trade.
evidence.limits: Washed downstream while still outfitting in a Bremen shipyard before taking on cargo.

evidence.title: Newport Late Medieval Basque/Atlantic Merchantman (Wales)
evidence.dateBasis: Dendrochronology (felled Basque Country after winter 1449 CE) and 1465 French brass coin sealed in keel scarf.
evidence.summary: Exceptionally preserved >25 m clinker-built Iberian/Atlantic wine & iron trader lost on the River Usk slipway while refitting, preserving Portuguese ceramics, corks, and rigging hardware.
evidence.limits: Upper decks lost; reveals cross-Channel Iberia–Wales medieval maritime connectivity.

evidence.title: Mary Rose Tudor Carrack Warship (Solent, England)
evidence.dateBasis: Historical Battle of the Solent loss date corroborated by coin series and dendrochronology of 1509–1536 builds/refits.
evidence.summary: Henry VIII's 45 m carvel-built vice-flagship capsized in battle preserving >19,000 Tudor artefacts: bronze & wrought-iron ordnance, yew longbows, surgical chests, compasses, and multi-ethnic crew skeletons.
evidence.limits: Port side preserved underwater in Solent silts while starboard side eroded away.

evidence.title: Godavaya Earliest South Asian Shipwreck (Southern Sri Lanka)
evidence.dateBasis: Wood radiocarbon (~2nd–1st c. BCE) and carinated Black-and-Red Ware / raw glass & copper ingots at 33 m depth.
evidence.summary: Oldest documented deep-water shipwreck in the Indian Ocean (~1st–2nd c. BCE), carrying raw cobalt-blue glass ingots, copper/iron ingots, querns, and Indian-Sri Lankan pottery off ancient Godapavata port.
evidence.limits: Hull wood heavily concreted/eroded beneath metal/stone cargo concretions.

evidence.title: Phanom-Surin Arab/Persian Sewn-Plank Wreck (Gulf of Thailand)
evidence.dateBasis: Organic geochemistry of Persian bitumen-lined West Asian torpedo jars, Pahlavi inscription sherd, and hull AMS dates.
evidence.summary: Over 25 m stitched-hull Western Indian Ocean trader excavated in Bangkok-delta mangrove clays bearing Khuzestan/Iraq bitumen torpedo jars, Guangdong stoneware, and Indian beads—proving early Abbasid–Tang monsoon trade before Belitung.
evidence.limits: Buried inland today by Chao Phraya delta progradation; bow/stern damaged in modern shrimp-pond digging.

evidence.title: Belitung (Batu Hitam) Abbasid–Tang Sewn-Plank Dhow (Indonesia)
evidence.dateBasis: Changsha kiln ceramic bowl inscribed '16th day of the 7th month of the 2nd year of Baoli reign' (826 CE).
evidence.summary: Indian/Arab coconut-coir sewn-plank vessel (Afzelia africana timber from East Africa/Arabia!) carrying ~60,000 Changsha bowls, cobalt-blue Abbasid/Tang wares, imperial gold cups, and star anise back toward Basra.
evidence.limits: Initial 1998–1999 commercial recovery predated full in-situ recording of every hull timber.

evidence.title: Intan & Cirebon Five-Dynasties Java Sea Wrecks (Indonesia)
evidence.dateBasis: Southern Han lead coins (c. 918–940 CE), Fatimid rock crystal/Syrian glass, and Yue celadons in lashed-lug hulls.
evidence.summary: 10th-century Southeast Asian lashed-lug traders connecting Java's Mataram/Srivijaya networks with South China ceramics, Sumatran tin, Middle Eastern blown glass, and Indian bronze ritual fittings.
evidence.limits: Deep open-water Java Sea salvages yielded vast cargoes while hull timbers survived piecemeal.

evidence.title: Kadakkarappally Malabar Sewn-Plank Boat (Kerala, India)
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dates on Artocarpus hirsutus (anjali) hull timbers in coastal Kerala clay.
evidence.summary: Rare 21 m indigenous double-ended sewn/dowelled Malabar coastal cargo vessel preserved in ancient coastal lagoon silts near Alappuzha during Chola-era Indian Ocean trade.
evidence.limits: Isolated hull lacking associated ceramics leaves exact cargo provenance unconfirmed.

evidence.title: Esmeralda (Vasco da Gama's 2nd Armada, Oman)
evidence.dateBasis: Unique Portuguese Indio silver coins minted in 1499 and copper-alloy mariner's astrolabe off Al Hallaniyah Island.
evidence.summary: Earliest archaeologically verified European Age-of-Sail wreck in the Indian Ocean—Vicente Sodré's naus wrecked in a cyclone, carrying the oldest known Portuguese mariner's astrolabe and King Manuel I coins.
evidence.limits: Wave-swept shallow gullies scattered artillery, ballast, and coins while hull timber largely disintegrated.

evidence.title: Nanhai No. 1 Southern Song Porcelain Merchantman (Guangdong, China)
evidence.dateBasis: 1183 CE Chunxi lacquerware inscriptions, Southern Song copper coins, and >180,000 export ceramics.
evidence.summary: 30 m Southern Song Chinese ocean junk raised intact in a caisson with >180,000 Longquan/Dehua/Jingdezhen porcelains, ~200 tons of iron bars, gilded jewelry showing Indian Ocean links, and bulkhead compartments.
evidence.limits: Caisson museum conservation keeps microscopic sediment strata under active long-term excavation.

evidence.title: Quanzhou Bay Song Oceangoing Spice Junk (Fujian, China)
evidence.dateBasis: Latest Southern Song Xianchun copper coins (1271 CE) and wooden cargo labels from Houzhu Harbor.
evidence.summary: 34 m multi-layered pine/camphor watertight-bulkhead junk returning to Zaytun (Quanzhou) carrying 2.3 tons of Southeast Asian frankincense, ambergris, tortoise shell, cowries, and pepper.
evidence.limits: Excavated in tidal saltmarsh mud; upper decks missing above the 12 watertight bulkheads.

evidence.title: Takashima Seabed: 1281 Yuan-Mongol Invasion Fleet (Nagasaki, Japan)
evidence.dateBasis: 1281 Phags-pa script official military seals, Chinese ceramic ink-dates, and bulkhead hull remains off Takashima Island.
evidence.summary: Underwater naval battlefield of Kublai Khan's shattered 1281 invasion armada (Takashima Hulls 1 & 2, explosive tetsuhau iron bombshells, stone anchors, and mixed Southern Chinese/Korean shipbuilding.
evidence.limits: Typhoon-wrecked warships scattered across seabed rather than a single intact intact cargo vessel.

evidence.title: Sinan Yuan-Era Celadon & Coin Freighter (Jeollanam-do, South Korea)
evidence.dateBasis: Dated 1323 CE wooden shipping tags (mukgan) binding Kyoto Zen temple orders sailing from Ningbo toward Hakata.
evidence.summary: 34 m Chinese bulkhead merchantman wrecked off Sinan carrying ~20,661 Longquan & Jingdezhen ceramics, ~28 tons of Chinese copper cash coins (~8 million coins!), red sandalwood logs, and spice jars.
evidence.limits: Bow & stern eroded in strong tidal currents; cargo preservation enabled near-complete manifest reconstruction.

waves.title: Bronze Age Copper & Tin Trunk Lanes (Levant–Cyprus–Aegean)
waves.summary: East Mediterranean copper-tin-resin trunk routes traced by Dokos, Kekova/Kumluca, Uluburun, Cape Gelidonya, and Point Iria wrecks.
waves.limits: Schematic sea-lane reconstruction linking excavated Bronze Age wreck points.

waves.title: Phoenician, Greek & Punic Western Mediterranean Sea Lanes
waves.summary: Sewn and shell-first merchantmen and naval fleets spanning Tyre/Carmel, Kyrenia, Sicily (Egadi), Massalia (Jules-Verne), and Iberian silver/tin shores (Mazarrón).
waves.limits: Schematic corridor connecting excavated Archaic–Hellenistic wreck sites.

waves.title: Roman & Late Antique Amphora-and-Art Trunk Routes
waves.summary: Industrial-scale Roman grain, Campanian wine, marble sculpture, and lead bullion transport documented by Madrague de Giens, Antikythera, Mahdia, and Pisa–San Rossore.
waves.limits: Representative trunk trajectory; secondary coastal routes omitted.

waves.title: Indian Ocean Monsoon & East China Sea Ceramic Highways
waves.summary: Direct monsoon-driven exchange linking Gulf/Arabian sewn dhows, Sri Lankan & Kerala ports, Nusantara entrepôts, and Song-Yuan Chinese porcelain junks.
waves.limits: Synthesizes multi-century monsoon circuits across Godavaya, Phanom-Surin, Belitung, Nanhai I, Quanzhou, and Sinan.

waves.title: North Sea, Channel & Baltic Sewn-to-Clinker-to-Cog Corridor
waves.summary: Northern European maritime engineering sequence from sewn war canoes (Hjortspring) and Romano-Celtic barges (Blackfriars, Zwammerdam) to Viking clinker ships (Oseberg, Skuldelev), Hanseatic cogs (Bremen), and Tudor carracks (Mary Rose).
waves.limits: Connects flagship excavated northern wrecks across 1,900 years.

studies.title: Shipwrecks of antiquity: sunken cargoes across the Old World
studies.summary: Trace 48 dated shipwrecks and sunken fleets across the Mediterranean, Black Sea, Nile, Red Sea, Northern Europe, Indian Ocean, and East China Sea—from Khufu's solar barque and Bronze Age copper freighters to Uluburun, Kyrenia, Antikythera, Belitung, Nanhai I, and the Mary Rose.
